The statement least likely to follow from Savigny's Volksgeist is any claim that law is a product of a sovereign's command, or a universal, rational code imposed top-down regardless of a people's history and customs. Savigny held that law grows organically out of a people's shared spirit and customs, so Austin-style command theory and Thibaut-style codification both contradict it. No options came through with your question, so I'm matching against the general view and can't confirm which listed statement that is.

CONFIDENCE: 40
